Location: Zoom
Attendees: Alicia Moran (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Leah Kim (Redwood CSM); Mark Chen (Praxis Head of AI), Rina Patel (Cloud Eng), Samir Gupta (Security Lead), Olivia Park (Product PM)
summary: Discovery focused on Dedicated capacity for Praxis Bank: reserved GPU pools for low-latency inference, isolation requirements for regulated PII data, burst strategy for peak trading hours, autoscaling and canary rollout expectations. Security/compliance (SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS) and pilot next steps discussed.
transcript:
[00:00] Alicia (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros - I'm Alicia Moran, AE for Redwood. Diego is our solutions engineer.
[00:08] Mark (Praxis): Hi all, Mark here, Head of AI at Praxis. We run a mix of customer-facing chat and internal scoring models, mainly inference.
[00:13] Rina (Praxis): Rina, cloud eng, will own infra ops.
[00:16] Samir (Praxis): Samir, security.
[00:19] Olivia (Praxis): Olivia, product.
[00:21] Diego (Redwood SE): Great, thanks. Goal today is to understand your latency/cost constraints and where Dedicated makes sense vs Hosted or Private.
[00:30] Mark: We're evaluating Redwood because our current self-hosted infra is getting expensive and we want predictable performance. Primary ask: reserved GPUs for production inference with strict isolation for regulated PII data.
[00:41] Alicia: Helpful. Can you give rough qps and token pattern? Burst windows?
[00:46] Mark: Baseline is about 50 qps across a handful of endpoints, peaks up to 300 qps during market open for a 10-15 minute window. Average sequence length 60-80 tokens, some longer customer transcripts 300 tokens.
[01:02] Diego: Okay that informs GPU selection and batching. For Dedicated we typically size by sustained throughput; for those 300 qps peaks you can either provision larger reserved pool or use burst capacity. Do you have constraints around overprovisioning cost vs accepting higher tail latency?
[01:19] Olivia: We can't have latency spike beyond 300 ms p95 for customer-facing flows. For internal scoring, 1s p95 is fine.
[01:27] Rina: Also, mandated isolation - model inference on dedicated GPUs that are not multi-tenant, and network isolation via our VPC. We want control plane traffic through our private peering.
[01:37] Alicia: That's exactly what Dedicated and Private options address. Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools under Redwood tenancy but isolated to your account; Private is fully customer-managed control plane. For your compliance, sounds like Dedicated with VPC peering might be the right fit, unless you need on-prem air-gap.
[01:55] Samir: We're SOC2 in scope, and we'll need KMS integration for keys, audit logs forwarded, SAML SSO for RBAC. Also need data residency in US-only regions.
[02:07] Diego: We support KMS and HSM integrations, SAML/SSO for provisioning, and audit log streaming. We'll share the security pack. One note: logging and some debug traces can be optionally redacted to avoid PII persistence.
[02:19] Mark: Nice. On autoscaling - we need a deterministic behavior for the burst. If we have a sustained peak for 10 minutes, what's Redwood's approach?
[02:27] Diego: Two patterns: 1) Reserved pool sized for baseline with configured burst capacity enabled to spin up extra nodes (subject to capacity availability) - best for cost efficiency. 2) Reserve upfront for peak (more expensive but deterministic). We also support scheduling scale policies to pre-warm for known windows.
[02:41] Olivia: Pre-warm sounds ideal for market open. Can you pre-warm and then scale down quickly?
[02:46] Diego: Yes, we can pre-warm. Pre-warming usually takes a few minutes depending on image and model warm-up; you can bake pre-warmed nodes with KV cache primed to reduce cold start latency.
[02:57] Mark: You mentioned KV cache - be careful, we have privacy concerns around cache persistence.
[03:02] Diego: Right, KV cache can be ephemeral per-session and is configurable; for regulated data we recommend disabling cross-customer caching and enforcing in-memory only with TTLs.
[03:11] Samir: Encryption at rest for model artifacts and data is mandatory, and we need proof for encryption in transit. Also, retention of logs - 90 days internal, 365 for audit.
[03:21] Alicia: We'll include details in the security pack. Quick question on models: do you host our own fine-tuned models or use Redwood's model catalog?
[03:29] Mark: We want to run our fine-tuned LlamaX models and some open models.
[03:33] Diego: Dedicated supports customer model uploads and pinning versions. We also provide quantization/compilation recommendations to optimize cost/latency tradeoffs. Sometimes transcriptions note 'Llama' as 'Lama' but just FYI.
[03:44] Olivia: (laughs) noted.
[03:46] Mark: For cost modeling, what's the unit pricing - reserved hourly + data egress?
[03:51] Alicia: Pricing is typically a monthly reserved capacity fee + per-token inference usage for overage/burst. We'll send exact tiers but example: 4x A100-equivalent GPUs reserved vs on-demand burst at higher unit cost. We can also do committed spend discounts.
[04:06] Rina: How do upgrades/rollouts work? We need canary and A/B splits and automatic fallback if latency or error rate crosses threshold.
[04:14] Diego: We have rollout primitives: canary deploy, traffic splits, and automatic fallback to a compatible model variant or hosted fallback if Dedicated capacity is exhausted. Rollouts integrate with tracing for per-route telemetry.
[04:26] Mark: Good. Any limits on concurrent KV cache sessions or batch sizes?
[04:30] Diego: We recommend batch sizes tuned to latency SLOs; continuous batching helps throughput but increases tail. We can provide benchmark numbers for your sequence lengths.
[04:40] Olivia: Our success criteria for pilot: p95 latency < 300ms for customer flow, cost per 1M tokens below our current baseline by 20%, and no data residency or isolation gaps.
[04:52] Alicia: Great, we'll aim the pilot to validate those. Next on security, Samir, anything else?
[04:57] Samir: We'll need an architecture diagram, encryption attestation, and a runbook for incident response. Also, penetration test results if available.
[05:06] Diego: We'll share architecture and SOC2 docs; pen test reports can be provided under NDA.
[05:11] Mark: Benchmarking - we'd like Redwood to run a small benchmark with our test harness to validate latency and throughput on a recommended Dedicated config.
[05:18] Diego: Absolutely. Typical workflow: you share test scripts or a recorded traffic trace, we run benchmarks on recommended instance sizing, and iterate on quantization and batching settings.
[05:26] Rina: For networking - VPC peering is preferred, private peering and customer-managed subnets. We also require private egress for model updates.
[05:34] Alicia: We support VPC peering and private link options; model downloads can be restricted via signed URLs and customer KMS.
[05:40] Olivia: Any common gotchas customers hit when moving from hosted to dedicated?
[05:44] Diego: Main ones: under-sizing for burst windows, not accounting for model warm-up time, and forgetting to disable cross-tenant caching for sensitive data.
[05:53] Mark: Pricing approvals will need to go to procurement. Samir will validate security pack.
[05:58] Samir: Yes.
[06:00] Alicia: Quick recap of next steps: I'll send pricing and SLA doc, Diego will run instance/cost recommendations and sample benchmark plan, Samir will compile security questions. We'll aim to have pilot kickoff week of 3/16 pending approvals. Anything else?
[06:14] Olivia: Please include example SLOs and runbook for rollbacks.
[06:18] Alicia: Will do. Thanks everyone.
[06:21] Mark: Thanks, really helpful.
[06:23] Diego: Thanks - we'll follow up with the artifacts.
[06:26] (call ends)

Notes: occasional transcription artifacts - 'KV cash' instead of 'KV cache' in one spot; 'Llama' sometimes transcribed as 'Lama'. Attendees used both role titles and first names. The conversation included explicit next steps and pilot success criteria.
